_meta.note: The advisor module's strings, merged over layer zero's pack of the same language at load (sdk/i18n.py `register`). Every key starts with `advise.`.

strings.advise.why.model_season: season (crop model): no {crop} cultivar matures before frost 8 years in 10 — the best in {share:.0%} of years
strings.advise.why.season_implausible: season: PLANTS lists {need:.0f} frost-free days, implausible for an annual — not used
strings.advise.why.season_perennial_range: season: PLANTS lists {need:.0f} frost-free days, from its perennial range; as an annual it needs only its time to harvest, which PLANTS does not give
strings.advise.why.season_short: season: needs {need:.0f} frost-free days, has {have} (8 years in 10)
strings.advise.why.season_little_short: season: PLANTS lists {need:.0f} frost-free days, has {have} (8 years in 10) — a little short
strings.advise.why.winter_below_listed: winter: average low {low:.0f} °F, below the {tmin:.0f} °F PLANTS lists
strings.advise.why.winter_near: winter: average low {low:.0f} °F is within {margin:.0f} °F of its {tmin:.0f} °F limit
strings.advise.why.water_irrigate: water: {rain:.0f} in of rain, needs {need:.0f} — irrigate
strings.advise.why.water_wet: water: {rain:.0f} in of rain, wetter than its {most:.0f} in maximum
strings.advise.why.ph_lime: pH: topsoil {ph}, needs {need} or more — lime
strings.advise.why.ph_sulfur: pH: topsoil {ph}, needs {most} or less — sulfur
strings.advise.why.texture_coarse: soil: PLANTS lists it as not adapted to coarse-textured soil
strings.advise.why.texture_medium: soil: PLANTS lists it as not adapted to medium-textured soil
strings.advise.why.texture_fine: soil: PLANTS lists it as not adapted to fine-textured soil
strings.advise.why.waterlogging: drainage: poorly drained soil, no tolerance of waterlogging
strings.advise.why.salt: salt: topsoil {ec} dS/m, low salt tolerance
strings.advise.why.paddy: water: grown flooded — needs a field that holds a flood (a tight subsoil, levees) and water to fill it; the season is not the limit here
strings.advise.title: What grows at {lat:.4f}, {lon:.4f}
strings.advise.preface: Generated {date} from open data. These are starting points, not answers: check them against local knowledge, a soil test, and your own records.
strings.advise.site.climate: Climate class {koppen}; average {mean:.1f} °C; {rain:.0f} mm of rain a year; USDA hardiness zone about {zone}.
strings.advise.site.frost: Last spring frost around {last} and first fall frost around {first}; at least {ffd} frost-free days in 8 years of 10.
strings.advise.site.heat: {gdd:.0f} growing degree days a year (°C, base 10); about {chill:.0f} chill hours in winter.
strings.advise.site.trend: Over the record, the later fifteen years were {change:+.1f} °C warmer than the earlier fifteen.
strings.advise.site.soil: Soil: {soil} — {drainage}, {slope}% slope; topsoil pH {ph}, organic matter {om}%.
strings.advise.site.nosoil: No soil survey at this point (it covers the United States). Use a soil test; ISRIC SoilGrids gives a worldwide estimate.
strings.advise.site.erosion: Left bare, this soil would erode at about {times:.0f} times the rate it can tolerate: keep it covered — cover crops, perennial forage, buffers.
strings.advise.site.caution: Climate is from NASA POWER's grid, tens of kilometres across: winter lows and frost dates in a field can be colder than shown.
strings.advise.section.crops: Food crops, simulated on this site's weather
strings.advise.crop.fits: {crop}: {fit} of {total} cultivars mature 8 years in 10, in {fast}–{slow} days. Sow {windows}.
strings.advise.crop.transplanted: Raised in a nursery and transplanted at {age} days: {fit} of {total}.
strings.advise.crop.fits_nowindow: {crop}: {fit} of {total} cultivars mature 8 years in 10, in {fast}–{slow} days.
strings.advise.crop.fails: {crop}: no cultivar matures before frost here.
strings.advise.section.fixes: Suits, with lime, sulfur or irrigation
strings.advise.bees.gaps: Nothing on the list is recorded in flower in {months}: plant for those months. (A gap can also be missing data.)
strings.advise.bees.nogaps: Something on the list is in flower in every month bees can fly.
strings.advise.livestock.heat: Dairy cattle face heat stress on {low:.0f} to {high:.0f} days a year: favour heat-tolerant breeds, shade and water.
strings.advise.nodata: {count} plants on the list have no data in either source yet — mostly fruit, herbs and flowers.
strings.advise.names_note: Plant names come from AGROVOC (FAO) and Wikidata where either has one in this language; the rest stay in English. The scientific name is always beside them.
strings.advise.sources: Climate: NASA POWER (CC BY 4.0). Soil: USDA NRCS soil survey (public domain). Plants: USDA PLANTS (CC0). Crop models: DSSAT (BSD-3-Clause). Bees: GloBI (CC BY 4.0) and the studies it cites. Fruit chill and heat: Fadón et al. 2020, Agronomy 10:409; González Noguer et al. 2023, Front. Hortic. 2:1217689; Fadón et al. 2023, Agronomy 13:518 (all CC BY 4.0); bloom frost thresholds: Washington State University via Penn State Extension. Plant names: AGROVOC (FAO, CC BY 4.0) and Wikidata (CC0).
strings.advise.why.invasive_here: listed as invasive or noxious in {state}
strings.advise.why.invasive_elsewhere: listed as invasive or noxious in {count} US state(s): {states}
strings.advise.future.title: The same farm, {label}
strings.advise.future.preface: The site's own thirty years of weather, every day {warm:+.1f} °C warmer and with {rain:+.0f}% rain — the delta method: today's ups and downs kept, their level moved. It does not model nights warming faster than days. Where the change comes from: {source}.
strings.advise.chill.preface: Winters here give at least {chill:.0f} chill hours (hours between 0 and 7.2 °C, November to March) 8 years in 10. Against published cultivar requirements — stone fruit compiled by Fadón and others (2020), apples by González Noguer and others (2023, the dessert and cider apples), pears measured by Fadón and others (2023) — taken in many countries and by several methods, so a guide, not a guarantee, this many cultivars of each would get their chill.
strings.advise.bloom.preface: Bloom and frost: for {count} cultivar estimates whose studies also give a heat requirement, bloom is simulated on this site's own winters — chill from November 1, then heat — and a year counts as frosted when the minimum falls to −2.2 °C (28 °F) or below within two weeks after bloom. The grid's minimums are milder than an orchard floor's, so the counts err low.
strings.advise.bloom.crop: {crop}: blooms {early} to {late} (median {median}); frost after bloom in {frost} years of 10.
strings.advise.bloom.crop_unmet: {crop}: blooms {early} to {late} (median {median}); frost after bloom in {frost} years of 10. For {unmet} of its {count} estimates, chill falls short in more than 2 winters of 10.
strings.advise.future.bloom: {crop}: median bloom {now} → {then}; frost after bloom in {fnow} → {fthen} years of 10
strings.advise.stamp: Made by fieldmesh advise {version}, data {data}, crop models DSSAT {dssat}.
strings.advise.nutrients.title: Manure and harvests
strings.advise.nutrients.supply: The animals' manure carries about {n:,.0f} lb of nitrogen, {p:,.0f} lb of phosphate (P2O5) and {k:,.0f} lb of potash (K2O) a year, as it leaves its handling system.
strings.advise.nutrients.removed: The harvests remove about {n:,.0f} lb of nitrogen, {p:,.0f} lb of phosphate and {k:,.0f} lb of potash a year from {acres:,.0f} acres:
strings.advise.nutrients.crop: {crop}: {n:,.0f} lb N, {p:,.0f} lb P2O5, {k:,.0f} lb K2O an acre
strings.advise.nutrients.acres_n: Spread at what the crops' nitrogen removal allows, the manure needs about {need:,.0f} acres; these crops have {have:,.0f}.
strings.advise.nutrients.acres_p: The soil test reads phosphorus high, so the plan is held to the crops' phosphate removal: the manure needs about {need:,.0f} acres; these crops have {have:,.0f}.
strings.advise.nutrients.caveat: A balance, not a recommendation: how much of the manure's nitrogen a crop gets in its first year depends on how and when it is spread, and what the soil needs depends on its own test. A state nutrient management plan governs.
strings.advise.nutrients.organic: Certified organic (7 CFR 205.203(c)): raw manure only on crops not for people, or worked into the soil at least this long before harvest:
strings.advise.nutrients.source: Sources: USDA NRCS Agricultural Waste Management Field Handbook, chapter 4 table 4-16(b) and chapter 6 table 6-6 (public domain).
strings.advise.propagation.preface: By the ways USDA PLANTS lists for each plant, in windows set by this site's median frost dates — common practice for each method, a first approximation. The plant-by-plant list is in propagation.csv.
strings.advise.propagation.seed_cold: Seed that needs cold ({count} plants): sow outdoors {windows} — the first after the fall frost, so winter stratifies it; the second for seed stratified cold and moist indoors.
strings.advise.propagation.seed: Seed ({count} plants): {windows}. Food crops with a crop model have their own sowing windows above.
strings.advise.propagation.container: Container stock ({count} plants), out of midsummer heat: {windows}.
strings.advise.propagation.sprigs: Sprigs and sod ({count} plants), in warm soil: {windows}.
strings.advise.fruitset.none: Heat that stops its fruit set — {day:.0f}/{night:.0f} °C by day and night over the {window} days before flowering ({source}) — does not come here: the warmest such stretch of nights in thirty years averaged {warmest:.1f} °C.
strings.advise.fruitset.days: Heat that stops its fruit set — {day:.0f}/{night:.0f} °C by day and night over the {window} days before flowering ({source}) — comes on about {days} days a summer, 8 years in 10: flowers opening then set little.
strings.advise.future.preface_cmip6: The site's own thirty years of weather, each month changed by the median of five CMIP6 models ({models}) between {hist} and {fut} under {scenario}: daytime highs {dmax_lo:+.1f} to {dmax_hi:+.1f} °C and nighttime lows {dmin_lo:+.1f} to {dmin_hi:+.1f} °C depending on the month, rain {rain_lo:+.0f}% to {rain_hi:+.0f}%. Today's ups and downs are kept; their level moves by month and by time of day. Projections: NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (CC0).
